title: Gravity and Colony Anew
premise: Casper Thackeray, a xenolinguist whose dreams have turned alien after years of contact work, discovers the name 'Vess Okafor' on the manifest of the Meridian, a colony ship that officially never launched. Following that ghost name, they are conscripted by a dissident archivist into proving the Kestrel Landing massacre occurred — an event erased from every official record aboard the orbital station Halcyon Reach. As Casper deciphers corrupted memory-cores and confronts their own complicity as a former records officer, they discover Vess Okafor was the child who survived, hidden inside the ship's linguistic archives. In the climax, Casper broadcasts the recovered testimony during the Meridian's reactor countdown, sacrificing their clearance and nearly their life; the truth fractures the station's manufactured consensus, and Casper, dreaming in human words again, helps the survivors' descendants claim their inheritance of memory.
about_author: Mirabel Iversen is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing distress calls before turning to fiction. They write about people who carry other people's words, and live somewhere with unreliable weather.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Casper runs a routine customs scan and finds 'Vess Okafor' listed on the manifest of the Meridian — a colony ship scrubbed from all registries. The emotional beat is quiet unease: a professional pattern-matcher recognizing a pattern that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Dreams in the Wrong Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Off-shift, Casper describes dreams conducted entirely in a language they helped catalog but cannot consciously speak — a side effect of deep xenolinguistic immersion. A station doctor offers memory-dampening treatment; Casper refuses. The beat is loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Digging into port archives, Casper finds the Okafor entry vanishes within hours of discovery — and someone has flagged their own query. A stranger slips them a data-chit in the cargo bay. The beat shifts from curiosity to hunted alertness.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Halcyon Reach
chapters.summary: POV Casper meets Sefa Ilori, a disgraced station archivist who claims the Kestrel Landing massacre — four hundred colonists — was not just forgotten but actively rewritten out of the record. She wants Casper's skills, not their courage. The beat is reluctant recruitment.

chapters.title: What the Records Agree On
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa shows Casper the seamless falsification: manifests, newsfeeds, even personal letters edited retroactively across thirty years. Casper recognizes the editorial hand — it matches training materials from their old records-officer corps. The beat is dawning complicity.

chapters.title: Cargo Run, Detour
chapters.summary: POV Casper. To reach the Meridian's sealed hulk in a decommissioned drydock, Casper takes a legitimate haul contract as cover, dragging their skeptical co-pilot Dree along. Customs interdiction nearly exposes them. The beat is tension under mundane routine.

chapters.title: Aboard the Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Inside the dead ship, Casper finds the linguistic archive intact — and hears a child's voice reciting phoneme drills in the dark. The reactor, impossibly, holds residual charge on a countdown cycle. The beat is awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: POV Vess (flashback). Thirty years earlier: nine-year-old Vess Okafor hides in the archive bay during the massacre, her mother sealing her in with the memory-cores. The beat is terror rendered through a child's taxonomy of sounds.

chapters.title: The Countdown Nobody Set
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Meridian's reactor, triggered by their boarding, begins a genuine countdown — a dead-man failsafe designed to destroy evidence if anyone comes looking. Sefa confirms: someone wanted this ship gone forever. The beat is a clock starting.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Language
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Working against the countdown, Casper decrypts the memory-cores using the same xenolinguistic methods they use on alien speech — treating the falsified record itself as a foreign text with telltale grammatical lies. First partial testimony surfaces. The beat is intellectual exhilaration.

chapters.title: Dree Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: POV Dree. Co-pilot Dree, waiting at the dock, starts pulling her own threads and realizes Casper's haul cover is impossible. Confronted, Casper tells her enough truth to endanger her. The beat is loyalty tested by honesty.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Signed
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The decryption reveals the falsification order was signed by Casper's former mentor, Commandant Reyes — the person who taught them that records are mercy. Casper must decide whether mentorship was grooming. The beat is grief for a hero.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa admits she helped build the original redaction system before defecting; her motive is penance, and she has been feeding Casper curated truths. Casper feels the ground shift. The beat is betrayal reframed as shared guilt.

chapters.title: Station Lockdown
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Halcyon Reach security, tipped by someone inside Sefa's network, seals the docks. Dree burns her own clean record to smuggle Casper back aboard the Meridian. The beat is friendship converted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Testimony, Fragment Seven
chapters.summary: POV Vess (flashback). Adult Vess, extracted from the archive years ago and silenced under a new identity, recorded fragment seven herself — she has been alive, adjacent, and afraid the whole time. The beat is the ghost becoming a witness.

chapters.title: Reyes Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Commandant Reyes boards the dying ship personally, offering Casper restoration, rank, and the dampening treatment that will end the alien dreams — if they walk away. The temptation is tailored precisely. The beat is seduction of forgetting.

chapters.title: The Grammar of a Massacre
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Alone with the cores while the countdown passes the point of no return, Casper completes the decryption: full audio, four hundred voices, timestamped against the forged logs. The proof is whole. The beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Casper. With minutes left, Casper hijacks the station's ceremonial band and broadcasts the testimony raw — no narration, just the voices. Reyes orders the reactor detonation; the crew refuses the order on open channel. The beat is the climax: truth outrunning authority.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: POV Dree. The countdown reaches zero and the reactor scrams — the failsafe's final clause required a willing hand, and no one aboard will give it. The Meridian survives as a monument. The beat is release after suffocation.

chapters.title: Hearings and Hollow Men
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Public inquiry begins; Reyes falls quietly, the system blames 'archival corruption,' and full justice stalls. Sefa testifies anyway, burning what remains of her career. The beat is victory that tastes incomplete.

chapters.title: Vess Okafor, Present Tense
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess steps forward publicly, reclaiming the name on the manifest, and meets Casper in the restored archive bay where she once hid. She asks Casper what her mother's voice said in the last core. The beat is inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Gravity and Colony Anew
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Months later, Casper ferries descendants of Kestrel Landing down to the re-founded colony, dreaming again in human languages — mostly. Some words stay alien now, and Casper keeps them, a private memorial. The beat is resolution: memory as a place you can finally land.
